Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: Unknown

Age: 75 years

Date of Admission: Unknown

Date of Discharge: Unknown
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Principal Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Clinical Presentation:

The patient, who had a medical history of hypertension, was admitted to the hospital with a complaint of fecal occult blood. A colonoscopy revealed a type II tumor in the sigmoid colon, which was located 23 cm from the anal verge. Histopathology of a biopsy specimen revealed moderately differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma. CT imaging showed sigmoid colon wall thickening, and regional lymph node metastasis was suspected. Blood examination showed an elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) concentration (32.7 ng/ml).

Hospital Course:

The patient underwent a laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy, which was performed without complications. Postoperative histopathological examination revealed moderately differentiated to mucinous adenocarcinoma, and three of the 16 retrieved lymph nodes contained malignant cells. The cancer was classified as stage IIIb [pT4a, pN1b, M0]. The patient was discharged after 10 days of recovery.

Treatment:

Following the diagnosis of stage III colorectal cancer, the patient was recommended to receive adjuvant chemotherapy with CAPOX starting 4 weeks after surgery. The selected regimen consisted of capecitabine and L-OHP. The anticancer drug dosage was reduced to 80% because of the patient's age. The patient also received 7.5 g of NYT daily throughout the course of adjuvant chemotherapy.

Outcome:

The patient did not report any significant adverse effects. Follow-up examination did not show any recurrence during a 1-year postoperative follow-up.

Discharge Condition:

The patient was discharged in stable condition with prescribed medications and follow-up appointment schedules.

Discharge Medications:

Detailed medication list not provided in the case report.

text:
**Principal diagnosis code: C18.7, Malignant neoplasm of the sigmoid colon**

**Rationale:**
- The tumour was found by colonoscopy in the sigmoid colon, 23 cm from the anal verge. Histology showed adenocarcinoma, and the sigmoid colectomy was the main treatment.
- It is coded to the sigmoid colon (C18.7), not the rectosigmoid junction (C19). A site 23 cm from the anal verge is well above the rectosigmoid junction, and the report calls it sigmoid colon throughout.
- The regional lymph node involvement (pN1b) and the absence of distant metastasis (M0) do not change the principal code. If you want to capture nodal spread, add **C77.2** (secondary and unspecified malignant neoplasm of intra-abdominal lymph nodes) as an additional diagnosis.
- The mucinous component does not change the site code. ICD-10-AM morphology (M-code) would be recorded as adenocarcinoma (M8140/3), or mucinous adenocarcinoma (M8480/3) for the mucinous component.
- Hypertension can be added as a secondary diagnosis (I10).
- The fecal occult blood was a presenting symptom and is explained by the cancer, so R19.5 is not coded separately.

**Possible additional codes:**
- C77.2 for the lymph node metastases
- I10 for hypertension
- Z51.1 for the encounter for chemotherapy, if the chemotherapy episode is coded separately (it would be a separate admission or episode from the surgical stay)
